transport: JSON-RPC 2.0 notification on the data plane: {jsonrpc:'2.0', method:'event', params:{type, seq, payload}}

envelope.seq: int >= 1, per session, allocated by core
envelope.x-vade: optional `x-vade.coalesce: true` on the frame — the event is droppable/self-contained (RFC-0007 §5.5 R5); a client MUST NOT treat a seq gap made only of such events as a hole.

rules: seq is allocated only by core, strictly +1 per session; clients never supply one.
Persist before broadcast: every event is written to `events` before it is queued to a UI sink, otherwise a reconnect replay has a hole.
Clients MUST de-duplicate by seq: a reconnect may deliver an overlapping segment.

Every turn's STATE-CHANGE event carries `state` (see turn.state): turn.queued, turn.started, turn.completed, turn.failed, turn.interrupted, turn.cancelled and turn.approval_resolved. turn.delta / turn.tool_call / turn.tool_result are payload-only and never carry `state`; a UI keeps the last state event and applies these deltas on top of it.
errors inside payloads use C-04 names only; no traceback ever appears in an event.
C3d may APPEND session.turn / session.closed (C-14); this file may not be rewritten by other batches.

RFC-0008 §6.4: a client that does not know an event type MUST ignore it and advance `last_seq` (never disconnect); a client that does not know a turn state MUST render it as `running`. `waiting_input` is the state this rule exists for (C-06 2.0.0 widened the enum).

session.attached.notes: First event a ui/attach caller sees. snapshot=false means from_seq+1.. is replayed contiguously; snapshot=true means the RPC result carried a snapshot and from_seq is its point.

payload.user_message_id: string (submit|edit: the new message; regenerate: the reused one)

turn.queued.notes: Emitted after the turn row and the user message are persisted.

payload.model_id: string (RFC-0005 append, optional; the id resolved at dequeue)
payload.model_source: session|global|priority (RFC-0005 append, optional; absent when no resolver is wired)

turn.started.notes: RFC-0005 append: `model_id` / `model_source` are OPTIONAL additions, emitted only once the turn resolved a model (see x-vade.rfc0005_append). `required` is unchanged.

payload.part_index: int >= 0, default 0 (RFC-0006 1.1.0; same value for every delta of one segment)
payload.kind: text|notice|reasoning|tool_args, default text (v1 core emits text|notice only)

turn.delta.notes: Concatenate in seq order; no delta is re-sent after a reconnect that was covered by replay.

payload.args_preview: string, JSON text, <=512 UTF-8 bytes, redacted (RFC-0006 1.1.0)
payload.started_at: int (unix ms, when core EMITTED this event)

turn.tool_call.notes: Only the digest goes to UI; full arguments travel in turn.approval_required for risk=high.

payload.duration_ms: int >= 0, or null when the tool did not actually run
payload.truncated: bool (summary window cut, or full text overflowed to the blob store)

payload.session_id: string (RFC-0007 §7.1: registered late — already on the wire)
payload.task_id: string|null (RFC-0007 §7.1: the task that raised the call; null = main turn)
payload.task_name: string <=80|null (redundant human-readable name, so a UI never shows a bare id)

turn.approval_required.notes: Broadcast to every attached UI. timeout = deny (fail-closed). RFC-0007 §7.1: `session_id` / `task_id` / `task_name` / `depth` are OPTIONAL additions (required is unchanged, old clients ignore them). A subagent's approval is broadcast in the PARENT session's stream: `session_id` is the parent, `turn_id` is the child turn and `task_id` names the task — the child session never has to be attached.

turn.approval_resolved.notes: The ONLY signal that closes dialogs on the other devices; must be broadcast even when the decision lost a first-wins race. When the resolved turn belongs to a subagent, `state` is the CHILD turn's state: a parent session that does not know that turn MUST ignore the state and close the card by `request_id` alone (RFC-0007 §7.2 rule 2).

payload.session_id: string (the seq space this event is broadcast on)
payload.schema: object (fixed descriptor per kind; NEVER a form DSL)
payload.options: array of {id,label<=120,description<=240|null}; 2..20 for choice kinds, [] otherwise
payload.default: string|string[]|bool|null (UI prefill ONLY; never applied on timeout)

turn.input_required.notes: RFC-0008 §6.1. Broadcast to every attached UI with the same input_id and payload; it carries `state:waiting_input`, so it IS the state-change event for entering that state (rule 4). Timeout = cancel: `default` never becomes an answer. Nullable keys are still written with a null value so the event describes itself.

payload.state: turn.state (the state this resolution restores: running, or interrupted)
payload.value: string|string[]|bool|null (non-null iff status=submitted, already validated by core)
payload.duration_ms: number (monotonic time from request to resolution)

turn.input_resolved.notes: RFC-0008 §6.2. The ONLY signal that closes an ask-user dialog: exactly one per input_id (§7.3 idempotency matrix), and it MUST be emitted before the turn's terminal event (S5). `by:'system'`+`status:'timeout'` and `by:<device>`+`status:'cancelled'` are the wire source of FR-8.55's 'did it time out'.

turn.completed.notes: state is exactly 'completed' (never 'done'). RFC-0005 append: the `usage` OBJECT gains `model_id` / `provider` / `source` / `steps` / `cached_tokens` / `reasoning_tokens`; the three frozen keys and the top-level `required` list are unchanged, so an old client that reads only prompt/completion/total keeps working.

turn.failed.notes: RFC-0005 append: `usage` (same keys as turn.completed.usage, `source="none"` when the provider never reported) and `data` are OPTIONAL; `required` is unchanged. A failed turn has burned tokens too, so they are accounted instead of vanishing.

turn.interrupted.notes: Emitted after tools/cancel is fired; core does not wait for the module. No turn.* event may follow this one for that turn. RFC-0013: the interrupted assistant's partial text is persisted as a `partial=true` assistant message that `partial_message_id` points at, so a fresh `ui/attach` snapshot contains it — replaying `turn.delta` is no longer the only source (FR-8.35). RFC-0005 append: optional `usage`, usually `source="none"` with zero counts because the provider had not sent a final usage yet — core does not estimate.

turn.cancelled.notes: Only for queued turns (ui/queue.cancel). A running turn is stopped with ui/interrupt, which returns INVALID_ARGUMENT for queue.cancel.

queue.updated.notes: Sent on every enqueue/start/finish/cancel so a UI never has to guess queue_pos.

module.status.notes: Emitted from registry changes through the same seq bus (C3 consumes registry, C2 produces the change).

payload.parent_id: string|null (parent TASK id, not a turn id)
payload.name: string <=80
payload.child_session_id: string|null (FR-8.58 jump target; null for kind=job)

task.started.notes: RFC-0007 §5.3. Exactly once per task, and BEFORE the spawning tool's turn.tool_result, so the activity list gets a row before the tool card collapses. Nullable keys are declared and required-with-null on purpose: every event is self-describing, so a consumer never has to walk back to task.started to rebuild the tree (§5.3).

payload.elapsed_ms: int (core-computed; never derive it from the device clock)

task.status.notes: RFC-0007 §5.3. Every state transition emits one, unthrottled. An action-text-only change is coalesced to at most 1/s (latest wins); nothing may follow the terminal task.finished for that task.

task.progress.notes: RFC-0007 §5.3/§5.4. Absolute value, never an increment; MUST NOT carry `state` (payload-only class, rule 4). Throttled to tasks.progress_hz (2/s) per task, coalesced inside the window with the LAST value kept, only emitted while a UI is attached, and the only class the session burst budget may drop. `x-vade.coalesce` means replay coverage may skip it and a client MUST NOT treat a seq gap consisting only of such events as a hole (§5.5 R5): the event is persisted and read_since still returns it, it is simply not a continuity witness.

payload.summary: string <=500 (subagent: final assistant text, truncated; job: result summary)
payload.forced: bool (true = the grace period expired and core stopped waiting)

task.finished.notes: RFC-0007 §5.3. Exactly once per task; the record is written before this is broadcast (§5.5 R1), and a late task.status/task.progress is dropped rather than resurrecting it (R2). `failed` MUST carry `code`; a cancel that hit its deadline MUST carry forced=true. `by` says who ended it, which is what separates 'the user stopped it' from 'its parent finished'.

turn.state.notes: Not an event: the enum every state-change turn.* payload's `state` takes. turn.delta / turn.tool_call / turn.tool_result do not carry it (see rules).

payload.user_text: string (the user message of that turn, verbatim)
payload.assistant_text: string (the final assistant message of that turn)

tool_calls.ok: bool|null (null while the outcome is unknown)

session.turn.notes: C-14 append. One event per finished turn, delivered only to role=evolve modules that are allowlisted, declare the topic and run with [evolve] allow_transcript=true. user_text and assistant_text are separate on purpose (AMEND-19): a consumer must never have to guess which side of a merged messages[] it is reading. `state` is terminal (completed|failed|interrupted|cancelled). turn.state carries no text, so a consumer that only sees it cannot build a turn.

session.closed.notes: C-14 append. Deliberately NOT the whole transcript and NOT a rolling summary: `tail` is the last 10 turns of original text, truncated by core, and the consumer accumulates its own summary in the same pass (AMEND-19). Best-effort: if the module is offline when the session closes, this one event is lost; v1 has no redelivery for session.closed (use session.turn with since_seq instead).

payload.name: string
payload.revision: int (the revision an approval would produce)
payload.base_revision: int (revision the proposal was authored against; 0 for create)

skill.proposed.notes: C-14 append. Metadata only: the body never travels here, otherwise a UI event would become a way to read unpublished skill text. Consumers: ui/admin front ends refreshing the pending list (C5a /skills). No session, so seq_from = seq_to = 0.

payload.degraded: bool (true only when the turn should have been refused but the ledger is untrustworthy)
payload.session_id: string|null (null for a core-wide day notification with no session context)

usage.budget.notes: RFC-0005 append (§6.4/§7.4). A notification, not the truth: `session/usage.get.budget.state` remains authoritative. Emitted at most once per (scope, state, period) — period is the session id for scope=session and the UTC date for scope=day — so a UI MUST de-duplicate by that triple after a reconnect. `state` is only `warn` or `exceeded`; `ok`/`off` never notify. `degraded=true` means exactly one thing: the budget was exceeded and `enforce="block"` would have refused the turn, but the ledger is untrustworthy (last measured turn had `usage.source="none"`), so the refusal was downgraded to a warning — it is never true for `warn`. Carries no token breakdown and no per-session detail for other sessions.

payload.reason: regenerate|edit_resubmit (fork reserved, never emitted in v1)

turn.superseded.notes: RFC-0006 1.1.0. Metadata edge, NOT a state: it carries no `state` and does not rewrite turn_states. Allowed to follow any terminal event for that turn (the terminal rule is exempted for this one event); clients de-duplicate by (turn_id, superseded_by) and ignore unknown types while advancing last_seq.

message.edited.notes: RFC-0006 1.1.0. Named `edited` but messages are immutable: the old row is never UPDATEd, it only gains `superseded_by`. `text` lets an attached client update the bubble without a re-attach; clients de-duplicate by superseded_by_message_id.

session.updated.notes: RFC-0010 append (§6.1). Emitted on the CHANGED session's own stream only, after a successful metadata write (session/rename, session/pin, session/archive, session/group.assign): a client attached to that session updates the row in place. A device that is not attached re-pulls session/list. Metadata edge, NOT a state change: carries no `state`, never reopens a turn. Nullable keys are written with null so the event describes itself.

payload.session_id: string (the session that was created or deleted)

session.list_changed.notes: RFC-0010 append (§6.2). Fanned out to EVERY attached session (module.status precedent) after a session is created (ui/attach auto-create, change=added) or hard-deleted (session/delete, change=removed); the changed session's own stream is skipped. Deliberately carries NO row payload — every client re-pulls session/list; a payload copy here would be a second truth that drifts. change=removed is the only notice a hard delete gives (§8.2).

payload.session_id: string (C-06 stream key; on subagent.* it always equals parent_session_id)
payload.parent_session_id: string (the seq space this family broadcasts on)
payload.parent_turn_id: string|null (the parent turn that spawned the run)
payload.child_session_id: string|null (the run's own LLM-loop session; FR-8.58 jump target)
payload.label: string 1..64

subagent.spawned.notes: RFC-0012 §5.2. Exactly once per run; emitted BEFORE any later event of the run on the PARENT session's stream. Payload-only class (no `state`): creation is the event name — a run is spawned, then `subagent.status` carries state changes. Nullable keys are required-with-null so every event self-describes without walking back (RFC-0007 §5.3 precedent).

payload.step: string <=120|null (what the loop is doing now)

subagent.status.notes: RFC-0012 §5.2. State-change event (C-06 rule 4). Required on every legal transition (spawned→running); during `running` the same event carries step/tool_name refreshes with state=running. Nothing may follow the terminal subagent.result for that run (a late status is dropped, not resurrected).

payload.result_digest: string (sha-256 hex of the FULL result text — NEVER the text itself; sha256("") for cancelled/failed-with-no-partial)
payload.result_chars: int (length of the full result text)
payload.error_code: C-04 name|null (core MUST set it when state=failed)

subagent.result.notes: RFC-0012 §5.2/§5.3. Exactly once per run; the record is written before this is broadcast. DESENSITIZATION RULE: the result text lives only in the child session's message stream — no `result_text`/`summary`/`output` key may appear here; consumers verify and reconcile by fingerprint. The FR-8.56 '≤500 字摘要' is the read-time `result_preview` projection of subagent/get, not a persisted or broadcast field.

payload.digest: string (sha256 hex over the catalog entries: name + clipped description + marker, name order)
payload.empty: boolean (true = the retirement entry: no skills are available this session)

turn.skill_catalog.notes: RFC-0003 §4.2/§5.1 row 6. Rides next to the persisted user-role catalog message (the `<system-reminder>` envelope; role=user, own seq). Sent on a session's first layered turn, when the digest changes (full replacement, no diff), and for the empty retirement entry — never twice for the same digest. Q1 answer, option (a): a client may render the paired message as a system notice instead of a user bubble.

payload.query_digest: string(12) (sha256 of the search query that surfaced it, empty when a skill's requires_tools enabled it)

turn.tool_discovered.notes: RFC-0003 §4.3.3/§5.5: sent once when a tool first enters the schemas() of a later step in this turn (tools/search hit or loaded-skill requires_tools). The same turn never repeats it for the same tool; tools resident from the turn's start never fire it. Unknown events are ignored by clients (RFC-0008 rule).

rfc0005_append.rewrites: none. Top-level `version` is NOT moved by this RFC (it reads 2.0.0 here because RFC-0008's enum widening owns that bump): core/tests/events/test_schema_append.py pins it, and RFC-0005 §7.4's proposed 1.1.0 bump is recorded here instead of by editing the frozen header. Every C-06 `required` list, rule, enum and turn_states entry is untouched; the only edits to existing entries are OPTIONAL payload keys plus notes. `usage.budget` is not a push topic (no `x-vade.push`), so the C-14 deliver gate ignores it.
rfc0005_append.why_sibling_key: A second append must not overwrite C-14's `x-vade.append` block; RFC-0006 uses `x-vade.appends[]`, RFC-0007 `x-vade.append_rfc0007`. This one is a named sibling so two RFCs can land in either order without a merge collision.
rfc0005_append.version_note: RFC-0005 §7.4 proposed `version: 1.0.0 -> 1.1.0`. Not applied: the append test pins the file's own version (now 2.0.0, owned by RFC-0008) and that field belongs to C-06, not to the appender. Recorded as a deliberate deviation in core/vade/llm/RESULT-rfc0005.md.

append_rfc0007.rewrites: none. Every pre-existing C-06 entry, rule and enum is unchanged; `turn.approval_required` / `turn.approval_resolved` gained four OPTIONAL payload keys (`session_id` / `task_id` / `task_name` / `depth`) and their `required` list did not move. `task_states` is a new TOP-LEVEL key, not an entry under `events` on purpose: only `turn.state` is exempt from the 'declared events nobody emits' gate, so a `task.state` entry would be red on day one (§9.2).

append.rewrites: none. Every C-06 entry, rule and enum above is byte-identical to the frozen 1.0.0 file; C3d has append rights only. `skill.proposed` is appended here too (v1.18 correction: C-14 carries three topics).

push_transport.emit_site: EventBus._dispatch(topic, ...) -- never SessionLog.emit(), so the C-06 static scan cannot see these three
push_transport.marker: each appended entry carries x-vade.push = events/deliver; tools/check_contracts.py scans _dispatch() and requires the marker on every pushed topic

topic_gate.session.turn: role=evolve AND (module_id, fingerprint) in [evolve] allowlist AND topic declared in manifest.subscriptions AND [evolve] allow_transcript=true
topic_gate.skill.proposed: role=ui|admin AND the topic declared in manifest.subscriptions; no transcript gate (no transcript in the payload)

deliver_envelope.transport: JSON-RPC 2.0 notification core->module: {jsonrpc:'2.0', method:'events/deliver', params:{topic, session_id, seq_from, seq_to, payload}}
deliver_envelope.seq_from: int: first seq of the source events this payload was assembled from (0 for topics with no session stream)
deliver_envelope.seq_to: int: last seq; a reconnecting module passes it as `since_seq` to resume
deliver_envelope.dedupe: exactly one delivery per (topic, session_id, turn_id); consumers MUST still de-duplicate by seq_to because a reconnect replay can overlap a live push (same rule as C-06).

redaction.owner: core config [evolve] redact; a module may not change it, and `redact: []` in a request is recorded as an override attempt, not honoured
redaction.flag: payload.redacted = true only when a field was actually replaced

backpressure.queue: one bounded queue per instance, 32 entries
backpressure.full: drop oldest and increment delivery_dropped; a slow evolve module must never stall a session
backpressure.on_failure: delivery_failed, no retry (v1 is best-effort; reconnect + since_seq is the recovery path)

overrides: turn.interrupted.notes: partial 同时落库为 partial=true 的 assistant 消息，turn.delta 不再是唯一来源
turn.tool_call.notes: 未脱敏完整参数仍只走 turn.approval_required；该事件另带脱敏预览
terminal rule: turn.superseded 允许跟在任一终态事件之后（元数据边，不是状态变化）
unknown event types MUST be ignored while last_seq advances

enum_widen.breaking: only for clients that validate every state against a frozen enum

overrides: turn.input_resolved is the only signal that closes an ask-user dialog
turn.input_required carries state:waiting_input and is therefore a state-change event
appends.rewrites: none. Every C-06 1.0.0 entry, rule and enum value above is unchanged; this batch only widens `turn_states` and appends two events (`version` moves to 2.0.0 because an enum widening is breaking for exhaustive validators).

overrides: turn.completed.usage: the OBJECT gains model_id/provider/source/steps/cached_tokens/reasoning_tokens; the three frozen keys stay
usage.budget is a session event, NOT a C-14 push topic (no x-vade.push marker)
appends.rewrites: none. The top-level `version` stays 2.0.0 (RFC-0008's enum widening owns that bump; this batch appends no state). Every pre-existing `required` list, rule and enum is untouched — the only edits to existing entries are OPTIONAL payload keys plus notes. Recorded in full under `x-vade.rfc0005_append`.

overrides: session.updated is a metadata edge: it carries no `state` and must not be treated as a turn state change (C-06 rule 4 does not apply)
session.list_changed is a session-stream fan-out (module.status precedent): clients re-pull session/list instead of maintaining the list from the payload
appends.rewrites: none. Top-level `version` stays 2.0.0: no enum widening, no state added — both events are new declarations and every pre-existing entry is unchanged. Neither is a C-14 push topic (no x-vade.push): both travel as session events through SessionLog.emit.

overrides: top-level `subagent_states` key appended (task_states precedent): a NEW top-level key, not an entry under `events` — only `turn.state` is exempt from the 'declared events nobody emits' gate (RFC-0007 §9.2)
subagent.spawned is payload-only (no `state`); subagent.status / subagent.result are state-change events (C-06 rule 4)
the family broadcasts on the PARENT session's stream: session_id == parent_session_id on every event; the child session need not be attached (FR-8.58)
DESENSITIZATION: subagent.result carries sha256(result text) + length, never the text; no result_text/summary/output key may appear on any subagent.* event (RFC-0012 §5.3)
appends.rewrites: none. Top-level `version` stays 2.0.0: no enum widening — `subagent_states` is a NEW top-level key and every pre-existing entry, rule and enum is unchanged. No x-vade.push on any of the three: all travel as session events through SessionLog.emit. Partially supersedes RFC-0007 §4.2's 'do not send subagent.*' for the subagent half (jobs keep task.*; see RFC-0012 §8).

overrides: turn.interrupted.notes: the 'partial text is reconstructable only from turn.delta events' sentence was deleted in place — since RFC-0006 §4 the text is persisted as a partial=true assistant message and a fresh ui/attach snapshot contains it (RFC-0013 §6; FR-8.35/R9)

this block is an explicit deviation from the RFC-0006 §9.3 'never rewrite notes bytes' rule: the stale sentence had become harmful (clients implementing from the notes discarded the persisted partial message); the RFC-0006 overrides entry above stays as audit history
appends.rewrites: turn.interrupted.notes only. No payload key, required array, rule, enum or turn_state changed. Top-level C-06 stays 2.0.0 (the enum bump is RFC-0008's); this block continues RFC-0006's 1.1.0 partial-pointer lineage at 1.2.0 — append-level, non-breaking.

overrides: turn.skill_catalog travels next to a persisted user-role `<system-reminder>` message (RFC-0003 §4.2); the message itself is an ordinary message row with its own seq, replayed like any other
turn.tool_discovered is payload-only: it never carries `state` and never changes the turn enum
RFC-0003 §5.5: unknown events are ignored by clients while last_seq advances (the RFC-0008 rule already covers this; restated here because both events land in one batch)

top-level `version` stays 2.0.0; `turn_states` / `task_states` untouched (RFC-0003 adds no state); both events are payload-only turn-stream writes emitted by core/vade/loop/engine.py in layered mode only
